caveats._: Hand-added 2026-09-05 AFTER the run. Documentation only: no numeric key in this file has been altered. This is a PRE-REGISTERED result (criterion: a difference is real only if the paired 95% CI excludes zero) and must not be re-run or amended post-hoc. Full record: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-sam3-spike-parity-measurement-findings.md
caveats.verdict: NULL. paired_extras_per_frame mean +0.4375, 95% CI [-0.4375, +1.4375], sign p = 0.34 -- the CI includes zero, so the pre-registered criterion is NOT met. average_precision: ours (a) 0.530 beats spike (b) 0.472.
caveats.matcher: Scored with the SHIPPED core/inference/semantic/calibration.py match_one_to_one, since discovered to be biased: its containment gate tests _centroid, the MEAN OF POLYGON VERTICES, which falls OUTSIDE 128 of 805 (15.9%) of these ground-truth ant outlines, vetoing near-perfect masks (verified case: IoU 0.904, matching area, unclaimed, scored a miss). On these SAME predictions a plain IoU>=0.5 matcher gives recall 0.868 -> 0.962 (a) and 0.852 -> 0.935 (b), and extras/tile 0.20 -> 0.07; ~65% of the 'extras' counted here are already-labelled ants whose match was vetoed. Both checkpoints move together, which is what a shared harness defect predicts. Deliberately NOT re-run under a corrected matcher: changing the metric after seeing the result is a post-hoc protocol change. This is also why extras_per_frame_at_target_recall is null for both -- target_recall 0.9 is unreachable anywhere on the confidence grid under this matcher.
caveats.contamination: Held-out frame 'f008975' is in checkpoint_b's OWN training set (the spike trained on fold_all, train split {f008078, f008161, f008975}). It was NOT dropped, because a post-hoc frame-set change is itself a protocol deviation. It is the single largest per-frame divergence (+6; next largest -3) and supplies most of the point estimate. Sensitivity excluding it: n=15, mean +0.0667, 95% CI [-0.600, +0.667] -- still null.
caveats.data_confound: This is NOT an adapter-surface parity test. checkpoint_b's fold_all dataset is 3 source frames / 108 tiles / 177 instances, and its train and valid splits are the SAME 108 files (no held-out set at all). checkpoint_a's is 62 frames / 2232 tiles / 3286 instances -- a ~19x difference. Any difference between these checkpoints is dominated by training data.
caveats.checkpoint_a_surface: checkpoint_a (20260904-143950) was trained on the OLD 206-module LoRA adapter surface, NOT the 312-module surface created on branch codex/sam3-spike-parity. That surface has zero training evidence; plan RUN A and RUN B were never executed.
caveats.granularity: The primary statistic is paired_extras_per_frame (n=16 source frames). paired_extras_per_tile (n=576) is secondary and correlated: tiles overlap 25%, so the same ant is scored in several tiles. Only 169 of the 576 tiles carry labels; on the other 407 every detection scores as an extra by construction.
